summary.text: The combination integrates random search, Bayesian optimization, and prediction to perform query-efficient black-box adversarial attacks on neural network classifiers. Initial input-output pairs are randomly chosen from a search space, after which a Gaussian process and acquisition function optimize perturbation inputs based on model prediction outputs.

target_user.text: The target user includes companies and researchers performing query-efficient black-box adversarial attacks on neural network classifiers, as indicated by patent filings and open-source active fine-tuning packages.

jtbd.text: When evaluating the robustness of neural network classifiers under black-box settings, the user wants to efficiently find adversarial perturbations with minimal queries so that they can test model vulnerabilities without exhaustive random searching.

value_prop.text: By replacing unguided search with a Gaussian process model and an acquisition function, the system reduces the query budget required to discover successful adversarial perturbations against neural network classifiers.

riskiest_assumption.text: The lowest-scoring DVF axis is Desirability (score 1.0) dvf:9. The riskiest assumption is that security practitioners and machine learning engineers will adopt a Bayesian-optimization-driven attack framework instead of relying on standard heuristic or random search methods for robustness testing.

mvp.text: To test the riskiest assumption on Desirability dvf:9, set up a demand landing page outlining the Bayesian-optimization-based adversarial testing framework and conduct structured problem interviews with machine learning security engineers.
mvp.type: demand landing page and problem interviews

success_metric.text: Achieve a proposed threshold of 25 percent conversion on the demand landing page and confirm that a proposed threshold of 80 percent of interviewed engineers report query inefficiency as a primary bottleneck in current robustness evaluations.

kill_criteria.text: If fewer than a proposed threshold of 10 percent of landing page visitors register interest, or if more than a proposed threshold of 70 percent of interviewed engineers state they have no need for query-efficient black-box attack optimization, terminate the project.

open_source.use: Provides active fine-tuning routines and utilities to manage iterative query loops and data selection.
Offers infrastructure for black-box optimization and hyperparameter search tasks.
Supplies PyTorch libraries for active learning feedback loops during model evaluation.

to_build.text: A specialized Gaussian process acquisition loop that integrates random search initializers with upsampled perturbation generation for target classifier queries.
